poems:
5:00.
The coffee maker starts on its timer,
faithful as a dog nobody feeds.

5:01. The first passenger of the route boards,
spoiled for choice.

The gym unlocks.
Two cars in the lot,
parked as far apart as the lot allows.

Dough doubled overnight.
It doesn't know.
Somewhere a mat goes down, facing the direction it always faces.
Alarm labeled DO NOT SNOOZE.
The night nurse writes her last set of vitals and gets the number wrong twice.
Ingredients: flour, water, salt, yeast, and one person awake at 5:07.

Cold tile.
Bare feet.
A decision made in one second
and unmade in two.

Only one bulb on, the one over the range.
Enough to make coffee by.
Discipline: doing at 5:10 what you decided at 10:40 last night.
Two treadmill belts, out of sync.

Thirty days.
The chip is the size of a poker chip
because that is what it is.

The dog is up because you are up.
The dog believes this was his idea.
A man in a reflective vest waits at the crosswalk with no traffic in either direction, and waits.
Steam off the pool. Lane four already taken.

5:16. The email surfaces mid-lather.
Nothing can be done about it until eight.

Proof.
Punch down.
Shape.
Rest.
In the oven by 5:40.

Someone's father is putting on
work boots he has owned
longer than his marriage.

Parking lot lamps still burning
well past their usefulness.
Overheard in the stairwell: I said five, I meant five, I am here, where are you.

Egg whites, no salt.
He does not like it.
He is not doing it to like it.
A kettle giving up on being polite.
5:23, and the driver has been awake three hours longer than her first passenger.

The birdbath holds exactly what fell in it.
No takers yet.
Hymn on the car radio, then an ad for gutter guards, then the hymn again.

Two hundred feet of hallway buffed last night.
First shoe print at 5:26.

He counts reps out loud
in an empty room
because the room is empty.
Bakery back door propped with a milk crate.

The new plan started Monday.
Odds are good this is not Monday.

The first batch goes in.
The street will know in twenty minutes.

Squeak of nurse's shoes
down the fourth floor,
stopping at the fifth,
where they put the carpet.
Somewhere a rooster is wrong about the time.
Oatmeal. Microwave. Ninety seconds. Stir. Ninety more.
The stationary bike in the basement is holding a shirt, a towel, and no rider.

5:35. The paper hits three porches in a row,
thrown by somebody's oldest.
Newspaper against the storm door.

Prayer rug, one corner turned up.
The coffee beside it going cold, because the coffee came second.
The kid with swim practice is already in the car, asleep against the belt.

Serving size one scoop.
Servings per container: about 33.
Amount per serving at 5:39: whatever you needed.

Loaves in, timer set.
Forty minutes of nothing to do, and no chance of doing it.

The fifth floor gets quieter now,
which is not the same thing as better.

5:42. Lunch made standing up,
the good leftovers claimed by the early riser.
The first customer at the drive-through window has been waiting since 5:41.
Chalk in the knurling, nobody in the room.

Quarter to six.
The people who set alarms for six are having their best fifteen minutes.

The baby went down at four.
Do not, under any circumstances, close a cabinet.
5:47, the exact minute the mind proposes moving to a smaller town.
Boots by the door, mud from a field that is either frozen or not.

5:49. A transfer slip dropped at the curb,
spent.

Ten minutes.
Enough for eggs or a shower.
History suggests the shower.

The custodian's radio,
one station, low,
the same station for nineteen years.

The woman on the rowing machine says nothing to the woman on the next rowing machine.
This is the friendship.

Elsewhere, dinner: someone orders
the second course without guilt.

Curtain still drawn.
Behind it, whatever the sky is doing.

Five minutes.
You can do anything for five minutes, which is the problem.
Rice cooker clicks to warm.
The first shower of the house begins, and the water heater begins its opinion.

5:58. The mirror gets wiped with a forearm
and asked for a verdict.
One eye open, negotiating with six o'clock.
